correctness.rationale: For every real parameter, a finite ball-residence bound follows from integrating an explicit pointwise polynomial derivative. For negative parameter P=z-ax has derivative y²-a>0; at zero parameter z has derivative y² and Cauchy–Schwarz controls x. For positive parameter the linear function G has derivative a+a^{-1}-r²+x²+(z+y/a)², forcing finite residence strictly below the equilibrium radius. Solving the three equilibrium equations gives exactly two at the threshold. Integrating x, P and G over compact stationary measures proves the radial defect and equality support condition. Rechecked the critical square decomposition using independently executed symbolic algebra; finite checks are corroboration, not substitutes for this argument. Risks: the result does not assert completeness of unbounded solutions or the existence of periodic cycles.

Conversely, the new theorem does not prove original numerical claims of chaos or periodic bifurcations; no stronger covering theorem was located.

originality.rationale: The actual same-equations original and two close follow-ups were inspected by full-text analysis. The 2014 original provides equilibria and numerical bifurcation evidence; the 2015 follow-up provides symmetry, Lyapunov data, and attractor pictures; the 2017 follow-up introduces a modified equilibrium-plane vector field. None of their relevant theorems or discussions bounds residence times or proves the sharp minimum ball radius and stationary second-moment equality for the original system. Semantic searches of published mathematical records using its monomials, aliases, residence time and moment statements found only different-flow analogues, none implying the stated sharp theorem. Absence from searched records cannot establish exhaustive priority; this residual risk is stated explicitly.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be proved by indexing; a differently notated or unindexed bound for the same ODE could exist.
The 1997 general low-term quadratic-systems paper was not inspected in full; its restricted stated scope and different field were considered without asserting whole-text noncoverage.
No theorem of existence of a chaotic set for any parameter is claimed.

value.rationale: The optimized Euclidean-ball residence boundary is a natural global geometric invariant of the exact flow introduced to exhibit an attractor/repellor pair. It is not merely the already known equilibrium-radius calculation: the result rules out arbitrarily long nonstationary transients uniformly below that radius, including the critical parameter at which no strict linear Lyapunov function is available, and characterizes equality in the associated stationary moment obstruction. The threshold escapes to infinity as the positive parameter tends to zero, giving rigorous context for the original numerically described cycle born near zero. The result does not require a paper-sized chaos theorem to have structural value.
